To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the capital structure of a firm is a determinant of its cost of capital and that the optimal capital structure of a levered firm is the one that minimizes the firm’s overall cost of capital.
the capital structure of firms is affected by the tax treatment of interest payments, and that the effect is stronger for small firms than for large ones.

(1) a firm's capital stock is composed of a number of assets with differing durability, (2) the firm's capital budgeting process is based on the net present values of alternative investments, (3) the firm's investment incentives are a function of the tax system and are therefore a function of asset life, (4) the tax system influences the composition of a firm's capital budget, and (5) the firm's optimal capital budget is a function of asset lives.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(a) the capital stock is a function of the rate of profit and the rate of discount, (b) the rate of profit is a function of investment incentive, and (c) the rate of discount is a function of inflation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the investment tax credit is a good tax instrument for promoting capital accumulation, and that the investment tax allowance is a better instrument for stimulating investment in short-lived capital goods.
the use of investment incentives is not justified.

the investment tax credit is a more efficient instrument than accelerated depreciation for encouraging capital formation, and that the investment tax allowance is a more efficient tool for encouraging capital formation than the investment tax credit.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the optimal capital allocation policy is not necessarily the one that allocates capital in the same proportion as the firm’s marginal products, and that it can be optimal to distort the allocation of capital in favor of the most productive projects.
there are many ways to allocate capital efficiently.
the optimal tax system is not necessarily the one which minimizes deadweight losses.
